result_text:
The emoji regex is now a single character class, `^[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Emoji_Component}]+$`, in both v4 (`packages/zod/src/v4/core/regexes.ts`) and v3 (`packages/zod/src/v3/types.ts`). A single class has no alternation for the engine to split across, so a failed match no longer backtracks exponentially.

- **ReDoS check:** I ran `recheck` with each pattern's real `source` and `flags` over every exported `RegExp` and every factory output you listed (`emoji`, `mac`, `uuid`, `string`, `time`, `datetime` across the argument ranges). All came back safe. That was a throwaway test, which I deleted afterwards, so there's no permanent test in the repo for this.
- **Tests:** I updated the expected strings in `continuability.test.ts` (the issue `pattern`) and `to-json-schema.test.ts` (the JSON Schema `pattern`) to the new form. The tests with "emoji" in their names pass. I did not run the full suite.
- **Not measured:** I didn't time rejection of `"🦰".repeat(26) + " "` directly, and I didn't separately run the `"🦰🦱🦲🦳"` accept case or the mixed-string reject cases. The class matches the same set of characters as the old alternation, so the accepted strings should be unchanged.
